anchor: Fermigier-Mestre parameter 28917/20, twenty certified Kummer classes
primary_hypothesis: For an odd prime p of good anchor reduction with v_p(D(u))=1 and p-integral unit u, the exact local obstruction subspace on the inherited anchor span is generated by the single root character at theta=1/u modulo p. A zero character is allowed: the claim concerns equality of subspaces, not a mandatory nonzero cut.
predictor: Evaluate the anchor point Kummer character x(P)-theta at the simple residue root theta=1/u. At a point reducing to that root use f'(theta); at reduction to O use the trivial character. Use only the anchor curve, its fixed class witnesses, u and the already certified prime support.
primary_endpoint: Exact agreement of predicted and existing local obstruction row spans at every eligible new prime on all six nonzero fibres. One mismatch refutes the rule as stated; ineligible primes remain outside scope.
secondary_endpoints: Separate inherited-bad-prime and new-bad-prime local constraints, including their row-space overlap.
Compute intersections of all inherited locally admissible spaces in the fixed twenty-dimensional coordinate system.
Compute pairwise and joint intersections of the embedded restricted CT radicals. A restricted radical is only a necessary solubility condition.
Keep cross-pairing against each full available class space when restricting to a common local subspace; do not replace it with the weaker pairing of that common subspace with itself.

layers.CT_annihilator: solubility obstruction, not a rational witness

boundaries: The inherited twenty-class space was built retrospectively from anchor points. This is not a point-blind selector on the R17/MW16 production families.

No local-space or restricted-radical dimension is an upper bound on the full curve rank.
